lessons.title: Language: Work-related Phrasal Verbs
objectives: Nắm vững các khái niệm và định nghĩa cốt lõi của Language: Work-related Phrasal Verbs.
Hiểu và áp dụng thành thạo các quy tắc và công thức trong SGK 12.
Rèn luyện kỹ năng phân tích và giải quyết các bài toán/tình huống thực tiễn ôn thi THPT & ĐGNL.

concepts.definition: Combinations of Verb + Adverb + Preposition that act as a single semantic unit (e.g., look forward to, come up with, run out of, keep up with). They are inseparable and always take an object.
concepts.example: Young graduates must keep up with technological advancements in their profession.
concepts.essence: Idiomatic authenticity in natural spoken and written English discourse.

concepts.definition: Education focused on practical skills and hands-on preparation for specific trades and technical careers, offering direct pathways into the workforce.
concepts.example: Many school-leavers choose vocational colleges for culinary arts or automotive mechanics instead of 4-year academic degrees.
concepts.essence: Practical workforce readiness aligned with immediate industrial needs.

rules.statement: Object placement with separable phrasal verbs
rules.meaning: With separable two-part phrasal verbs (take on, fill out), if the object is a pronoun (it, them), it MUST go between verb and particle: fill it out (NOT *fill out it*).
rules.example: Here is the application form; please fill it out carefully.
rules.essence: Rhythmic constraints of English phonology prioritizing weak pronoun stress internally.

workedExamples.prompt: Replace the underlined phrase with an appropriate phrasal verb: 'She decided to start learning graphic design to improve her job prospects.'
steps: Step 1: 'start learning an activity/hobby' translates to phrasal verb 'take up'.
Step 2: Replace: She decided to take up graphic design to improve her job prospects.

commonMistakes.mistake: Placing pronouns after inseparable or three-part phrasal verbs: *I look forward to meet you*.
commonMistakes.why: 'To' in 'look forward to' is a preposition, which must be followed by a noun or gerund: look forward to meeting you.
